title: Idaho's 2nd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District pits 14-term Republican incumbent Mike Simpson against Democratic nominee Elinor Gilbreath, along with Libertarian, independent, and Constitution Party candidates. Simpson, first elected in 1998, chairs the House Interior and Environment Appropriations Subcommittee and has fended off primary challengers with 63.3% of the vote in the May 19 Republican primary. The district, rated R+13, covers eastern Idaho and northern Boise, and Simpson has won general elections by wide margins for decades. Gilbreath, a Ketchum lawyer and mediator, ran unopposed in the general Democratic primary after Julie Wiley withdrew, and is campaigning on restoring constitutional balance, protecting public lands, and lowering costs for Idaho families.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls were found for this race as of the research date. Major nonpartisan forecasters (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) rate the district as 'Solid Republican' or 'Safe Republican.'

candidates.name: Mike Simpson
candidates.summary: Mike Simpson is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 1998 and now seeking a 15th term. He chairs the House Interior and Environment Appropriations Subcommittee and is a former Speaker of the Idaho House of Representatives, with a career spanning over 40 years in elected office. Simpson describes himself as a pragmatic conservative focused on affordability, energy independence, and farm workforce reform, and he has raised over $900,000 for his 2026 campaign.

candidates.name: Elinor Gilbreath
candidates.summary: Elinor 'Ellie' Gilbreath is a lawyer, mediator, and the Democratic nominee for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District. A Ketchum resident of 23 years, she has spent over two decades working with businesses, civic leaders, nonprofits, schools, and communities on conflict resolution and complex decision-making. She defeated Julie Wiley in the May 19 Democratic primary with 72.5% of the vote and is campaigning on restoring constitutional checks and balances, protecting Idaho's public lands and water, lowering costs for families, and keeping public lands in public hands.

forecast.rationale: No independent public polling exists for this race, which caps confidence at medium. However, the structural indicators are overwhelming: Idaho's 2nd is an R+13 district, major nonpartisan forecasters (Cook, Inside Elections, Sabato) all rate it Solid/Safe Republican, and 14-term incumbent Mike Simpson has won general elections by wide margins for decades while chairing a powerful Appropriations subcommittee. Simpson raised over $900,000, defeated primary challengers with 63.3%, and faces a Democratic opponent (Elinor Gilbreath) who ran unopposed in her primary in a district with a deep Republican lean. The field also includes multiple minor-party and independent candidates, which may further dilute the Democratic vote share. All available evidence points to an overwhelming Republican advantage.
